Follow-up to #341. CodeRabbit's review of 354c0e9 left one non-blocking finding: [scripts/prove-check-generator-drift-revert.ts:71](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-changelog/pull/341#discussion_r4536757507). Normalize CRLF to LF before the multiline mutation seams are matched, so the revert proof also works on a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`. Add a test that feeds a CRLF copy of the source and fails on revert.

---

### GitHub comments (1)

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-13T06:07:18Z)
>
> Two Minor findings from the final review of pm-changelog#341 (head 37cc0bb), deferred here under that PR's last-full-round rule:
> - **PRRT_kwDOSfkApc62-Tap**, `scripts/prove-check-generator-drift-revert.ts:256`. For mutation cases that select another test file, the fixed and restored controls run only `test/check-generator-drift.test.ts`. A target that already fails would count as a detected mutation. Each case must require its own test file and pattern to pass before the mutation and after restoration.
> - **PRRT_kwDOSfkApc62-Tat**, `src/check-drift.ts:136`. The PowerShell copy of the regeneration command single-quotes each argument, and Windows PowerShell 5.1's legacy native-argument passing then drops embedded double quotes (for example `title: 'Notes "quoted"'`). Either escape for that interpreter or require PowerShell 7.3+ with `$PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing = 'Standard'`. The copied-command test must check the exact reproduced option, not only `/Notes/`.
Follow-up to #341: normalize line endings before the drift revert proof matches multiline seams
